title: Classroom Activities · Mindful Eating
chapter_focus: Understanding food groups, balanced diets, and healthy eating habits.

activities.title: Plate Builder
activities.objective: Plan a balanced meal using locally available foods.
materials: Printed paper plates (one per student) with empty sections
Food picture cards (rice, dal, sabzi, curd, fruit, salad, ghee, milk, etc.)

steps.title: Set up
steps.detail: Spread the food cards on a central table. Each student takes a paper plate.

steps.title: Build
steps.detail: Each student picks cards to fill a balanced plate that includes carbs, proteins, fats, vitamins/minerals, and fibre. They paste the cards on the plate.

steps.title: Tag
steps.detail: Beside each card, the student writes which food group it represents and one nutrient it provides.

steps.title: Show and tell
steps.detail: Five volunteers explain why their plate is balanced. The class asks one question per plate.

guiding_questions: Which food group was hardest to include? Why?
Did anyone forget a food group? Which?
Could you cook this meal at home? With what changes?
Could a meal be balanced with even fewer items?
variations: For older classes, add a 'budget' constraint — total cost must stay under a limit.
For mixed-language classes, let students label cards in their home language too.

activities.title: Iodine Detective
activities.objective: Use the iodine test to detect starch in different foods.
materials: Small samples of: boiled potato, bread, rice, sugar, salt, apple, paneer, milk

steps.title: Predict
steps.detail: Before testing, students predict which foods contain starch. Write predictions on the board in two columns.

steps.title: Test
steps.detail: In groups, students place one drop of iodine on a small bit of each food. Record colour change: blue-black = starch present; brown stays = no starch.

steps.title: Compare
steps.detail: Compare predictions to results. Cross out wrong predictions, circle right ones.

steps.title: Conclude
steps.detail: Each group writes ONE conclusion about which food groups tend to contain starch.

guiding_questions: Were sugar and starch both in the 'sweet' group of your prediction? Did the test agree?
Why did rice and bread give the same result?
What does this teach us about labels and food packaging?
What other simple test can detect fat?
safety_notes: Iodine solution stains skin and clothes — handle with care.
Do NOT taste any food after iodine has been added.
variations: Add lemon juice to a sample to see what happens (vitamin C reacts).
Compare two brands of bread — does whole-wheat have a different shade of blue-black?
